chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the servant repents with sincere repentance, Allah loves him, so He veils him in the world and the Hereafter.' So I said, 'And how does He veil him?' He said: 'He causes His two angels to forget what they had written against him from the sins, and He reveals to his limbs:
ai.seo_question: How does Allah conceal the sins of a person who repents sincerely?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elaborates on the concept of *satr* (divine veiling) by detailing a cosmic mechanism where Allah commands the recording angels, the servant's own limbs, and the earth itself to conceal specific sins, ensuring they do not testify against the repentant believer on the Day of Judgment. In Shia scholarship, this highlights the comprehensive nature of sincere repentance (*tawbah nasuha*), transforming not just the record of sins but the very physical and spiritual witnesses to them. It underscores the mercy of Allah in removing the burden of past transgressions entirely, allowing the servant to stand before Him with a clean slate.
